extracted.intended_audience: general readers and those interested in documentary films, media ethics, and BBC/Ofcom controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria relevant to producing and broadcasting a BBC-commissioned documentary (accuracy, impartiality, disclosure, translation, production process, financial transparency, and regulatory compliance). Applicable when assessing documentary editorial quality and broadcaster due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentary must adhere to the BBC's editorial rule on accuracy; the internal review determined the film breached this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Johnston's internal review faulted Hoyo Films for failures that led to accuracy breaches. The BBC's finding of 'serious flaws' in production cited accuracy concerns; the BBC removed the film from iPlayer pending further checks. Broadcasters should ensure factual correctness and clarity in presented content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of contributors' ties/conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Production companies and contributors must disclose relevant personal or familial connections (e.g., the narrator's link to a Hamas official).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC stated it had not been informed about the narrator's connection to Hamas; reviewers faulted Hoyo Films for not disclosing al-Yazouri's ties. Failure to disclose such ties can lead to removal, audits, and reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary content should comply with impartiality standards; internal review found no other breaches of editorial guidelines on impartiality in this case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although accuracy breaches were found, Johnston's review found no breaches of impartiality and no evidence of improper external influence. Producers and broadcasters must judge whether coverage gives balanced perspectives in line with impartiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence / vetting of contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters and producers are expected to research and vet contributors' backgrounds before transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Danny Cohen and others criticised the BBC for not disclosing or researching the narrator's family links prior to broadcast. Proper vetting is part of editorial process and can prevent post-publication controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production process rigour
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentary's production processes must meet editorial standards and be free from 'serious flaws' in how the film was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC review found 'serious flaws' in the documentary's production process, prompting a full audit and internal review. Producers should follow robust production workflows, oversight and documentation to meet editorial requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Production expenditures, payments, and financial arrangements should be transparent and auditable (e.g., BBC demanded a 'full audit of expenditure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC paid £400,000 to Hoyo Films; Hoyo paid the narrator's mother £790. The BBC demanded a full audit after controversy. Transparent contracting and disclosure of payments to participants are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance: not materially misleading / maintaining audience trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcast content must not be materially misleading and must preserve audience trust; Ofcom found the film violated broadcasting rules and was 'materially misleading'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ofcom instructed the BBC to broadcast a statement with its findings. Broadcasters must ensure content does not mislead viewers in ways that could erode trust, or face regulatory sanctions and mandated corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and terminology accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations and word choices (e.g., rendering 'Yahud'/'Yahudy' as 'Israelis' vs 'Jews') should reflect intended meaning and conform to editorial guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Telegraph criticised translation choices; others argued the translation reflected intended meaning. The BBC editorial standards committee had previously determined 'Israeli' was an acceptable translation for 'Yahud' in some contexts. Translators and editors must apply guidance and consider nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic interrogation and inclusion balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about which voices and stories to include should avoid 'glaring' omissions and ensure appropriate journalistic questioning (e.g., pressing interviewees on sensitive views).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics argued the inclusion of adults' stories alongside children's stories led to omissions, such as not pressing a single mother on her views of the 7 October attacks. Editorial judgment should weigh humanising storytelling against necessary critical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant payments and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments to participants (honoraria, fees) should be recorded and disclosed appropriately as part of ethical and editorial transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports noted Hoyo Films paid £790 to the narrator's mother; such payments drew scrutiny. Clear records and disclosure of participant remuneration help assess potential conflicts and ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action and public accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters must take corrective action when issues are identified (e.g., removing content, performing audits, publishing review findings, issuing public statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC initially added a message, then removed the film from iPlayer to perform due diligence, commissioned a full audit and internal review, and later accepted Ofcom's ruling and was instructed to broadcast its findings. Timely, transparent remediation is required when standards are breached.
